caption: A 3D rendering of one right hemisphere with the object-responsive region (LO, red) drawn next to motion area MT/V5 (green) in the lateral occipital cortex.
notice: The red patch is the area that responded to pictures of objects in the fMRI scan, so this shows where activity tracks objects, which is a correlation.
short: Malach et al. 1995, Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A

caption: Group fMRI results on brain slices for touching the second finger versus the fifth finger (a) and the second finger versus the big toe (b); the color shows which stimulated body part contributed more to each activated voxel.
notice: Activation shows up around the lateral sulcus (LS) on both sides of the brain, which fits the card's point that S2 has a coarse body map that also appears on the ipsilateral side; this is a correlation.

caption: A drawing of the area removed from both medial temporal lobes, showing a medial view with the cingulate gyrus, corpus callosum, fornix, hippocampal gyrus, uncus and hippocampus, and the 5 cm and 8 cm removals.
notice: This marks which limbic structures were taken out in the operations after which memory was lost, so the link between this damage and amnesia is causal.
short: Scoville et al. 2000, J Neuropsychiatry Clin Neurosci

caption: Probabilistic maps of the corticospinal tract in coronal (a to g), horizontal (h to n) and sagittal (o to u) slices of a standard brain; warmer colors mean more of the postmortem brains had the tract at that spot.
notice: The red and yellow core shows where the tract reliably runs, and the blue edge shows how much its position varies between brains.

caption: Bias scores for areas of the medial temporal lobe; scores near 0 mean pattern separation and scores near 1 mean pattern completion.
notice: Only the CA3/DG bar sits near 0, so this region's activity leaned toward telling similar items apart while the other areas did not; this is a correlation from fMRI.

caption: Lesion overlap map for the Iowa Gambling Task (IGT), a value-based decision task, with the peak region circled and a bar graph comparing lesioned and normal participants.
notice: Patients with lesions in the circled ventromedial prefrontal spot scored lower than those with lesions elsewhere, so damage there causes the decision-making deficit.
short: Gläscher et al. 2012, Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A

caption: Activation maps on brain slices from individual subjects: voxels preferring objects defined by motion (light blue) or by texture (yellow), with the overlap in red.
notice: The red overlap in the lateral occipital region on both sides shows the same area responds to objects whichever cue defines them; this is a correlation.

caption: An axial cut through a brain specimen with arrows on the precentral knob, which looks like an inverted omega.
notice: The omega-shaped bulge of the precentral gyrus is the landmark the card describes for finding the hand area and the central sulcus.

caption: Electrodes over one participant's superior temporal gyrus (A), the sentence heard with its spectrogram (B), responses across electrodes over time (C), and one electrode's response to each phoneme (D).
notice: Electrode e1 responds mostly to the stop sounds (d, b, g, p, k, t), so a recording site is tuned to a group of speech sounds; this is a correlation.

caption: Brain specimens with the intermediate sulcus of Jensen traced in red, shown in bayonet, T or Y, and arcuate forms; the intraparietal sulcus is green and the superior temporal sulcus is blue.
notice: The red line has a different shape in different hemispheres and runs on from the intraparietal sulcus, matching the card's point that it branches from it and varies.

caption: Median change in seizure frequency from baseline over the three-month blinded phase for the stimulated (active) and control groups.
notice: The stimulated line falls to -40.4% while the control line rises back to -14.5%, so stimulation of the anterior nucleus is what reduced seizures; this is a randomized trial, which tests cause.

caption: Second-target accuracy against the delay between targets for three patients with pulvinar lesions, with separate lines for the Contra and Ipsi sides.
notice: For patients DG and CR the Contra line lies below the Ipsi line, so lesion damage is tied to worse performance on one side; this is a lesion result, which tests cause.
